summary.intent: Add Phase 27 (Writable Shares PoC) to the CipherBox roadmap and capture implementation decisions via a structured discuss-phase session, building on the insight that CipherBox's server-relayed IPNS architecture already solves the multi-writer coordination problem.
summary.outcome: Phase 27 was added to the roadmap with a cleaned-up slug, a CONTEXT.md was created capturing decisions across four gray areas (IPNS key delivery, write scope, share dialog changes, conflict & attribution), and STATE.md was updated with session info.

repo: CipherBox's conflict detection works because ALL IPNS publishes go through the API server, which acts as coordination point — sidesteps the general 'unsolved multi-writer IPNS' problem entirely
Optimistic concurrency via expectedSequenceNumber is checked server-side before every publish; two writers hitting a conflict get a 409, re-sync, and retry — same as multi-device sync today
Phase 14 established read-only sharing using secp256k1 public keys, share_keys table, and lazy key rotation on revoke — Phase 27 extends this pattern
The planning docs conservatively label multi-writer IPNS as 'unsolved' but this applies to the DHT/network layer, not CipherBox's server-coordinated architecture
Milestone 4 (TEAM-11) plans a formal cryptographic read/write key hierarchy; Phase 27 is a PoC that intentionally uses a simpler approach (ECIES-wrap the IPNS signing key alongside folderKey)

code.finding: expectedSequenceNumber check enforced server-side before every publish — the authorization point for sequence-based conflict detection
409 Conflict handling with automatic single-retry and re-sync logic
UI conflict banner with jitter-delayed retry
Sequence number comparison across network vs DB cache — highest wins
Phase 14 explicitly scopes to read-only sharing only; read-write sharing deferred as future phase
Access model design: readers get decryption keys only, writers (future) would get IPNS signing keys
Read-write sharing deferred because giving recipients IPNS private key enables re-sharing; multi-writer IPNS noted as unsolved
TEAM-11: cryptographic role enforcement via separate read/write key hierarchies so viewers literally cannot write
CRDTs require all writers to have the IPNS private key — only owner and write-sharing recipients should publish folder metadata

workflow: gsd-tools auto-generates slugs from full phase descriptions, which can produce absurdly long directory names — manual slug cleanup was needed after add-phase ran
The depends-on field in ROADMAP.md defaults to the previous phase number; for Phase 27 it needed manual correction to Phase 14 (the actual dependency)
discuss-phase workflow follows a structured four-area pattern: IPNS key delivery → write scope → share dialog changes → conflict & attribution
The branch was created before running /gsd:add-phase to isolate the work properly

friction: gsd-tools generated an absurdly long slug from the full phase description, requiring manual directory rename and ROADMAP.md edits after the fact
The auto-generated depends-on in ROADMAP.md pointed to Phase 26 instead of Phase 14 (the actual dependency), requiring a manual fix
STATE.md required two separate edits — one to add the Roadmap Evolution section and one to update content — suggesting the section didn't exist yet
open_items: Metadata-embedded IPNS key delivery (embedding wrapped signing key in folder metadata for decentralized key distribution) deferred to a future decentralization phase
Cryptographic read/write key hierarchy (Milestone 4 TEAM-11) is the proper long-term solution; Phase 27 is intentionally a PoC using ECIES-wrap approach
Re-sharing prevention (ensuring read-write recipients cannot reshare access) not addressed in this PoC — future phase concern
Conflict attribution in UI (showing who last modified when a conflict occurs) was discussed but exact implementation left to planner discretion
30s polling sync and tab-focus triggers already exist but behavior for read-write shared folders specifically may need validation
The general multi-writer IPNS problem at the DHT/network layer remains unsolved — Phase 27 works only because CipherBox routes all publishes through its own API
